clue.text: Fish stuffed with your butter brings a passionate exultation

indicators.note: a thing stuffed with something has it packed inside, so the fishing word is opened up

parts.note: to dib is to fish by letting the bait bob lightly on the water
thy is the old form of your
a ram is an animal that butts, so a butter

explanation.surface: A fish stuffed with butter seems to bring a diner great joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts: a ram. DIB is a less familiar verb for a style of angling.
explanation.definitionFit: A dithyramb is a wild, impassioned hymn or speech, originally sung in honour of Dionysus.

clue.text: Take greasy stuff out of paste — energy content lost

indicators.note: the energy symbol is lost from inside the word, from its content rather than its ends

parts.note: to paste someone in a contest is to beat them soundly, to defeat them
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An instruction to strip grease from a paste, with a remark about lost energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paste' looks like a noun in the kitchen but is the verb meaning to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: To defat meat or stock is to remove its fat, the greasy stuff in it.

clue.text: Concerning nutrition that could be offered by this unending crop

indicators.note: the letters available could be offered up in another arrangement, signalling a reshuffle
the word this loses its final letter, as something with no ending would

explanation.surface: A remark that a word about feeding could be supplied by a harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unending' trims THIS to THI, and 'could be offered by' rearranges THI with CROP.
explanation.definitionFit: Trophic is a biological adjective meaning relating to feeding and nutrition, as in trophic levels.

clue.text: Chatters with rising voice — should be keeping quiet

indicators.note: the reversed word keeps the quiet sign inside it
in a down clue a word that rises is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a say is a voice in a matter, as in having your say
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone talking with a rising voice when they ought to keep silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SAY into YAS, and 'keeping' holds P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To yap is to talk shrilly and incessantly, so someone who yaps chatters.

clue.text: Plant on the wall cut short, having grown up

indicators.note: in a down clue growing up means reading upward, so backwards
the word loses its final letter, so it is cut short at the end

parts.note: a mural is a painting placed on a wall

explanation.surface: A climbing plant that was trimmed back and has now grown up the wall again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes MURAL to MURA, and 'having grown up' reverses that to give the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Arum is a genus of plants with a hooded spathe, including cuckoo-pint, also called lords-and-ladies.

clue.text: Sort of time when one may have an awful shock?

definitions.text: Sort of time when one may have an awful shock?

parts.words: Sort of time when one may have an awful shock?
parts.note: a shock here is a thick mass of hair, so an awful shock is unruly hair, rather than a nasty surprise

explanation.surface: A question about the kind of day on which some dreadful surprise might strike.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'shock' of hair is a bushy tangle, so the awful shock is a mess on one's head, not a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a day when one's hair will not behave, and by extension a day when everything goes wrong.

clue.text: A few elders, perhaps, work before start of service in church

indicators.note: the work and the opening letter are placed in the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

indicators.note: the work comes before the next letter, side by side

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: only the opening letter of service is taken

explanation.surface: Some church elders working before a service begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elders' looks like senior churchgoers, but elder is a tree; a copse is a small group of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small stand of trees, and elders are trees, so a few of them may form one.

clue.text: Works around the offices at night, maybe, to establish blameless record?

parts.note: an office cleaner cleans the rooms, working around them
night is one example of a late hour

explanation.surface: An office cleaner on the night shift building an unblemished reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The office cleaner who CLEANS LATE gives the two words of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean slate is an idiom for a record with no faults or offences against one.

clue.text: A one-sided picture for the official records

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
a file is a collection of official records

explanation.surface: A partial portrait kept for the official files.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-sided' here means showing one side of the face, a side view.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is a side-view portrait, showing only one side of the subject's face.

clue.text: Phone-in doctor briefly sorted out painkiller

indicators.note: letters sorted out are put into a new order

parts.note: Dr is the short form of doctor

explanation.surface: A radio phone-in where the doctor quickly sorts out a pain remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges PHONEIN with DR.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorphins are hormones the body releases to relieve pain, natural painkillers.

clue.text: Imperial units to confound dopes badly mustered

indicators.note: soldiers badly mustered fall in out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Imperial measures that would baffle fools drawn up in poor order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly mustered' rearranges all fifteen letters of TO CONFOUND DOPES.
explanation.definitionFit: The foot-pound-second system is the old imperial set of units for length, mass and time.

clue.text: Goatlike animal will need that horn regularly trimmed

indicators.note: every other letter is trimmed away at regular intervals, leaving alternate ones

explanation.surface: A goat whose horn needs regular cutting back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly trimmed' keeps the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of THAT HORN.
explanation.definitionFit: The tahr is a wild Himalayan mammal related to goats.

clue.text: More refined daughter isn't ungrammatical? That is right

parts.note: ain't is the nonstandard form of isn't
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A daughter's improper grammar put right by someone more refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ungrammatical' asks for the slang form AIN'T, apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Dainty means delicate and refined, so daintier is more refined.

clue.text: Scallywag and gentleman fearful climbing mountain

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable rogue

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads upward, so the two words run backwards

parts.note: Sir is a gentleman's title
dire means dreadful, fearful

explanation.surface: A rogue and a frightened gentleman scaling a mountain together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns SIR plus DIRE into ERIDRIS. CADER IDRIS is a mountain in Snowdonia, north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Cader Idris is a well-known peak in the Snowdonia national park in Wales.

clue.text: See Pasquale so healthy turning up as an old chap

parts.note: Pasquale is the setter, who refers to himself as me
thus means so, in this way

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word upward, so backwards

parts.note: hale means robust and healthy

explanation.surface: The setter invites us to see him, still healthy, appearing as an old man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link inviting the solver to look; 'turning up' reverses HALE to ELAH. The setter's name stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah, the biblical patriarch said to have lived 969 years, is a byword for a very old man.

clue.text: Adventurer to encourage a listener in the audience

indicators.note: an audience hears, so the phrase is taken as heard

parts.note: to buck up is to encourage, and an ear is a listener, so buck an ear

explanation.surface: An adventurer cheering on someone listening in the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCK AN EAR, heard by the audience, matches the word. 'buck' as encourage comes from buck up.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer was a pirate, and the word is extended to any reckless adventurer.

clue.text: Closest friend embracing one in a sexually depraved way?

indicators.note: the friend phrase holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: your best ally is your closest friend
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A close friend's embrace that turns out to be indecent.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is a stretch: beastly behaviour read in its sexual sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestially means in a beastlike, brutish way, and in particular sexually depraved.

clue.text: Old doctor with lust ensnaring nurse, finally

indicators.note: the lust word traps the final letter inside it

parts.note: to lech is to lust lecherously

indicators.note: only the last letter of nurse is taken

explanation.surface: An old doctor whose lust leads him to trap a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old doctor' is an archaic term; physicians were once called leeches after the bloodsucking worms they used.
explanation.definitionFit: Leech is an archaic word for a physician, from the medical use of leeches.

clue.text: Composer's scornful work not given run

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the composer is the answer

indicators.note: the run letter is not given, so it is left out

parts.note: a satire is a work mocking its targets
r is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A composer's mocking piece that was never performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not given' drops R from SATIRE. Erik Satie was a French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer famous for the Gymnopédies.

clue.text: Fat man to fight for a food container

parts.note: Friar Tuck is the stout friar of the Robin Hood legend
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A stout man brawling over a food box.
explanation.walkthrough: A tuck box is the box of food and sweets British boarding-school pupils keep; tuck is school slang for snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuck box is a container for food, especially treats kept by a pupil at boarding school.

clue.text: Listen to what the tea lady has — internal disease, internal pain

indicators.note: the disease letters go inside the combined phrase

parts.note: to hear is to listen to
a tea lady serves from a large urn
TB is short for tuberculosis

explanation.surface: Hearing the tea lady's troubles: an internal illness, internal pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internal' is both the container signal and part of the surface's echo. A tea lady once served tea from a big urn in British offices and factories.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartburn is a burning pain felt inside the chest from acid indigestion.

clue.text: Lady I embarrassed? It's not spoken about

parts.note: Una is the lady of Spenser's Faerie Queene, also a woman's name
someone embarrassed goes red

explanation.surface: A lady's blushing over something kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady' asks for a woman's name: UNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaired means not voiced or discussed in public, so not spoken about.

clue.text: The thing (one sticking into part of body) that is most irritating

parts.note: it refers to the thing

indicators.note: the numeral sticks into the body part, inside it

parts.note: the chest is part of the body
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something stuck into the body, which is the most irritating thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticking into' puts I inside CHEST to make CHIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchiest is the superlative of itchy, describing what irritates the skin most.

clue.text: Pole's tactless remark putting English off

indicators.note: the English letter is taken off the word

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder or tactless remark

explanation.surface: A Polish speaker's blunder that offends the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole's' looks like a nationality; it is a pole, as a fishing gaff, with 's for is. 'off' drops E.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaff is a hooked pole used to land large fish.

clue.text: Given food — plant fodder eaten with nasty smell

indicators.note: the plant is eaten, taken inside the fed word

parts.note: fed means given food
the ti is a Pacific plant whose roots and leaves serve as food

explanation.surface: Fed with plant fodder that then gives off a nasty smell.
explanation.walkthrough: The ti, or cabbage palm, is a crossword favourite among plants for its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetid means smelling foul or rank.

clue.text: Tax cut of 50% for royal female

indicators.note: half the word, its first four letters, is cut away

parts.note: a princess is a female royal

explanation.surface: A tax cut of half applying to a princess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut of 50%' removes PRIN, half of PRINCESS. Cess is an old word for a local tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A cess is a tax or levy, an old word still used in Ireland and India.

clue.text: It's covering belonging to item of furniture

indicators.note: the sex appeal letters cover the possessive word, enclosing it

parts.note: it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA, with 's for is
of indicates belonging, as in the house of my father

explanation.surface: A cover belonging to a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' in crosswords often means sex appeal; 'covering' wraps those letters around the word for belonging.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered seat for several people, an item of furniture.

clue.text: Politician who could be creditable and moral

indicators.note: the letters could be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician who might be both reputable and upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges CREDITABLE and MORAL together. The Liberal Democrats are a British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberal Democrat is a member of the British centrist party of that name, so a politician.

clue.text: Line up for the mathematicians?

parts.note: read as a vertical line on a graph that runs up the page, not as people queuing

explanation.surface: Mathematicians queuing for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line up' sounds like a queue but is a vertical line, the upward axis of a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: On a graph the vertical axis, along which values are plotted upward, has the letter name.

clue.text: He had to get American group restricted and managed thriftily

indicators.note: the American group is restricted inside the contracted pronoun

parts.note: he'd is short for he had
US means American
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: He had to keep an American band on a tight budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted' puts USBAND inside HE'D, apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to use them carefully and economically.
